plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates how individual neurons in a shallow neural network define hyperplane decision boundaries in input spaces of increasing dimension, across three side-by-side panels labeled a), b), and c). Panel a) shows a one-dimensional input space with a horizontal number line labeled x_1 and a single point (the origin dot) marking where the linear threshold function crosses zero, representing a hyperplane as a point in 1D. Panel b) shows a two-dimensional input space with axes x_1 and x_2 and two colored lines passing through the origin: a vertical teal line and a horizontal orange-terracotta line, each representing a separate hyperplane boundary that divides the 2D plane into two half-spaces. Panel c) shows a three-dimensional input space with axes x_1, x_2, and x_3, rendered as a perspective cube with a light gray front face and teal side face, where the flat face of the cube represents a plane slicing through 3D space — the hyperplane in 3D. The figure demonstrates how the linear pre-activation of a neuron defines a hyperplane that separates input space into two regions, with the dimensionality of the hyperplane being one less than the input dimensionality.

elements: x1 axis: horizontal arrow pointing right, black, labeled x1
x2 axis: vertical arrow pointing up, black, labeled x2
x3 axis: diagonal arrow pointing lower-left toward viewer, black, labeled x3 (visible in 3D mode only)
origin dot: small black sphere at (0,0,0)
teal hyperplane: semi-transparent teal plane representing neuron 1's decision boundary (normal initially along x1)
orange hyperplane: semi-transparent orange-terracotta plane representing neuron 2's decision boundary (normal initially along x2)
positive-side shading: light tint on the w·x+b > 0 side of each hyperplane
negative-side shading: slightly darker tint on the w·x+b < 0 side of each hyperplane
draggable input point: colored sphere that the learner moves through feature space
classification indicator: small text or color-coded label showing the sign of each neuron's activation and the combined output
axis tick marks at integer positions along each visible axis

interactions.label: Input dimension
interactions.teaches: A neuron's decision boundary is always one dimension less than the input space: a point in 1D, a line in 2D, a plane in 3D

interactions.label: Weight w₁
interactions.teaches: Adjusting one weight component rotates the hyperplane's orientation — the boundary tilts because the normal vector w changes direction, altering which inputs are classified positive vs negative

Moving the input point through feature space reveals which side of each neuron's hyperplane it falls on; the final output class flips when the point crosses any boundary, showing how multiple neurons combine to partition space

demo_steps.title: 1D: hyperplane is a point
demo_steps.narration: In one dimension, the equation w₁x₁ + b = 0 has a single solution — the hyperplane degenerates to a point on the number line. The teal marker shows where the neuron's activation crosses zero.

demo_steps.title: 2D: hyperplane is a line
demo_steps.narration: In two dimensions, the boundary w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + b = 0 is a line. The teal line (neuron 1) and orange line (neuron 2) each split the plane into two half-spaces. Drag the point to see which region it occupies.

demo_steps.title: Tilt the hyperplane
demo_steps.narration: Slide w₁ from 1 to -1. The teal line rotates — its normal vector tilts, changing which inputs produce positive activation. The shaded regions swap sides.

demo_steps.title: 3D: hyperplane is a plane
demo_steps.narration: In three dimensions the boundary becomes a full plane slicing through space. Two neurons define two planes; their intersection creates four regions. Drag the point through 3D to see the combined classification.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World space: axes span ±3 units along each dimension. In 1D mode only x1 axis visible (horizontal line from -3 to +3). In 2D mode x1 horizontal and x2 vertical, both ±3. In 3D mode add x3 pointing toward viewer at ~45° below horizontal (matching panel c's viewpoint). Teal hyperplane: PlaneGeometry 6×6 units, color #7ecfc4 at 0.35 opacity, normal initially [1,0,0] (the x1=0 plane, matching the vertical teal line/plane in the source). Orange hyperplane: PlaneGeometry 6×6, color #c47a5a at 0.35 opacity, normal initially [0,1,0] (the x2=0 plane). When w1 slider changes, rotate the teal plane's normal to [w1, 1, 0] normalized (in 2D) or [w1, 1, 0] in 3D. Draggable point: SphereGeometry radius 0.12, color #ff6600. Positive-side shading: extend a thin colored slab 0.05 units thick on the w·x+b>0 side, teal-light #b2e8e2 at 0.15 opacity; negative side #5a9e96 at 0.15 opacity. Axis arrows: black lines with cone tips, radius 0.02. Origin dot: black sphere radius 0.06. Labels: x1, x2, x3 in black, positioned at axis tips. Colors from source: teal #7ecfc4, orange-terracotta #c47a5a, gray #b0b0b0 (unused in interactive version), black axes.
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.PlaneGeometry for hyperplanes and rotate via quaternion setFromUnitVectors when the weight slider changes. For the drag interaction, raycast against an invisible plane perpendicular to the camera through the point's current position to get smooth 2D screen-space dragging mapped back to 3D. In 1D mode, constrain the drag to the x1 axis only. Show/hide geometry groups per dimension toggle rather than rebuilding. The classification indicator should update reactively: compute sign(w·x+b) for each neuron and display +1/-1 badges near each plane, plus a combined output label. Use double-sided material for planes so they're visible from both sides.
